description: Fig. 7 is a composite 4x3 array of twelve bright-field TEM micrographs, panels (a)-(l), all recorded in two-beam diffraction near the [111] zone axis, each with a selected-area diffraction inset printed with its operating reflection g and "z=[111]", and each carrying a 500 nm scale bar. Panels (a)-(f) are labelled "10Al α" (ferrite of 10Al steel) and (g)-(l) "8Al α" (ferrite of 8Al steel). Dislocations are colour-annotated: red dashed = "Screw", magenta = "Mixed", blue = "Edge"; white dashed lines mark traces such as (010), (112), (101), (011), (211) and (111). In 10Al (a-f) the ferrite contains predominantly long, straight, non-uniformly distributed screw dislocations; contrast is lost for some operating vectors and recovered for others, giving g·b = 0 and b = a/2[111]. In 8Al (g-i) edge, mixed and screw dislocations coexist, again with b = a/2[111] from loss of contrast under two operating vectors. Panels (j)-(l) image the ferrite-austenite phase interface, where a darker band is labelled "γ"; edge dislocations activate readily at these boundaries. All dislocation types show planar slip in both steels.
measured_quantities: Burgers vector of ferrite dislocations (a/2<111> type)

observations.observation: All twelve panels are bright-field TEM micrographs, each with a 500 nm scale bar and a selected-area diffraction inset labelled z=[111].
Panels (a)-(f) are labelled "10Al α" and panels (g)-(l) are labelled "8Al α" in the top-left corner of each image.
Dislocation characters are colour-coded on the images: red dashed lines = "Screw", magenta = "Mixed", blue = "Edge".
White dashed trace lines in (c), (f), (i) and (l) are labelled with crystallographic planes including (010), (112), (101), (011) and (211).
Panels (j)-(l) show a darker band at the lower right labelled "γ" adjacent to the ferrite region labelled "α", i.e. the ferrite-austenite phase interface.
The caption states that the dislocation morphology shown is of ferrite after 3 % tensile deformation, with (a)-(f) for 10Al steel and (g)-(l) for 8Al steel.
The citing text states that the two-beam diffraction mode was used with the samples pre-deformed to 3 % engineering strain.

The citing text states that when g = [10-1] and g = [1-10] some long straight dislocations systematically lose contrast while for g = [0-11] all dislocations are visible, giving b = a/2[111] for the ferrite in 10Al steel.
The citing text states that in 8Al steel some dislocations lost contrast under the [011] and [1-10] operating vectors, also giving b = a/2[111] by g·b = 0 analysis.
The citing text states that the predominant fraction of dislocations in 10Al ferrite are long straight screw dislocations with a non-uniform distribution.
The citing text states that edge dislocations are more readily activated at ferrite grain boundaries (ferrite-austenite interfaces shown in Fig. 7(j-l)) because of high local stresses.
The citing text states that approximately 24.3 % austenite in 8Al steel acts as a soft phase alleviating stress localization in the ferrite.
The citing text states that edge, mixed and screw dislocations in ferrite of both steels exhibit typical planar slip character.
